paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: Jesus is never too busy and never too late. Jairus is begging Him to hurry, a crowd is pressing in, and Jesus stops for one woman who has spent twelve years and all her money on physicians (Luke 8:43). He calls her "Daughter" and sends her off in peace (Luke 8:48). If you ever feel like you're stuck at the back of the line, that's the Jesus who turns around and says, "Who touched Me?" (Luke 8:45).

Now look at what He tells Jairus when the worst news arrives. "Your daughter is dead," the messenger says (Luke 8:49). Jesus answers, "Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed" (Luke 8:50). I think Jairus's whole world just dropped out from under him, and Jesus doesn't ask him to understand it. He asks him to believe, and then He walks right beside him into that house.

The mourners laughed because they knew she was dead (Luke 8:53). They were right about what they could see, but they didn't know who was standing in the room. Jesus took her by the hand and said, "Child, get up!" and her spirit returned (Luke 8:54-55). So when your situation looks finished, friend, bring it to Jesus anyway, because He can do what nobody else in the room can do.
